catalog: A Massachusetts pharmacist completed the appropriate injection-training program and receives a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol in its single-dose presentation. The prescriber directs pharmacy administration, but the pharmacist's CPR certification expired last week. What is the best action under the current MH/SUD administration guidance?
A
Administer the dose because the medication, prescription, and repeat-dose requirements are otherwise satisfied
B
Administer the dose after obtaining an additional written patient consent acknowledging that CPR certification has expired
C
Postpone pharmacist administration until current CPR certification is restored, because current CPR certification is an administrator requirement
D
Administer the dose if another pharmacy employee with current CPR certification remains in the pharmacy during the injection
E
Administer the dose if the prescriber gives same-day verbal confirmation that the pharmacist may proceed despite the expired certification
A pharmacy schedules an intern for a shift without a pharmacist preceptor directing the work. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
A senior technician may serve as the preceptor.
The intern must work under direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.
Five hundred internship hours permit independent prescription verification.
Intern status does not authorize independent pharmacist practice.
The pharmacist preceptor remains responsible for the supervision relationship.

A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed the required administration training and maintains current CPR certification. Each option involves a medication that appears on the MH/SUD administration list. Which requests may proceed under the current guidance? Select all that apply.
A 34-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol supplied in its single-dose presentation
A 45-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for Invega Sustenna, but this would be the patient's first dose of the medication
A 39-year-old patient requests Abilify Maintena from anonymous pharmacy floor stock that is not tied to a patient-specific prescribed single dose
A 17-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Invega Sustenna
A 52-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Abilify Maintena supplied as the prescribed single dose
MA-CASE-0891

A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.
A trained pharmacist with current CPR administers an eligible single-dose LAI to an adult under a valid prescription and product requirements.
A qualified intern administers an eligible adult patient’s IM medication under appropriate pharmacist supervision.
A pharmacist immediately informs the prescriber after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A pharmacy documents patient consent, screening, lot, expiry, administration route/site, and administering professional.
A pharmacy administers ceftriaxone intravenously using the circular’s IM authorization.
MA-CASE-0962
A pharmacist uses the authority to administer a prescribed HIV-prevention injection as the basis for independently prescribing that injection.
MA-CASE-0958
A pharmacist uses a multidose supply as the basis for bypassing the circular’s single-dose packaging requirement.
A trained pharmacist uses the circular to administer the same LAI to a 16-year-old without another lawful authority.
A pharmacist checks medication-specific training and current competency before adding a newly eligible administration service.
MA-CASE-0579

A Massachusetts retail pharmacy offers medication administration under DCP 26-03-124. The cases do not involve a hospital privilege or a separately authorized opioid treatment program. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which ONE proposed handling is supported by the applicable requirements?
A pharmacy keeps only the insurance claim and omits the administration-specific patient and product records.
A pharmacist ignores applicable REMS because the state circular lists the active ingredient as eligible.
MA-CASE-0961
A pharmacist waits for the next routine progress report after an administration reaction requiring emergency-department monitoring.
A pharmacist follows labeling and applicable REMS for an eligible long-acting buprenorphine injection.
A certified technician uses this non-vaccine administration circular to give an adult patient a long-acting antipsychotic injection.
MA-EXP-0351

Case A: A technician qualified to vaccinate is assigned to administer a long-acting injectable antipsychotic under the general medication-administration circular.

Case B: A pharmacist proposes using that circular to administer an otherwise eligible medication intravenously to a 17-year-old.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.
Vaccination qualification does not place the technician within this pharmacist-or-intern medication pathway.
The limited individual MCSR exception for administration does not waive all pharmacy facility registrations.
The proposed intravenous administration to a 17-year-old does not meet this pathway's age and route conditions.
An eligible medication must also meet the specified single-dose packaging and prescription conditions.

A Massachusetts pharmacist administers a patient-specific dose of Abilify Maintena under the mental-illness administration pathway. Shortly afterward, the patient develops a severe reaction requiring emergency medical services and evaluation in an emergency department. Which follow-through actions are consistent with current Massachusetts guidance? Select all that apply.
Immediately report the adverse event to the prescriber because emergency-department treatment is one of the specified serious outcomes
Record the adverse outcome or adverse event in the pharmacy's administration record
If the event is a dispensing error or a serious adverse drug event, fulfill the pharmacist's or intern's applicable Board reporting responsibility
Delay prescriber communication until the next routine reassessment because the patient has already been transferred to emergency care
Omit the event from the pharmacy record when emergency medical services create their own clinical documentation

A pharmacist discovers that an improper warfarin dispensing caused a patient to be hospitalized, and the facts meet the serious-injury reporting criteria in 247 CMR 20.02(1). Which statements correctly distinguish the duties triggered by this same event? Select ALL that apply.
The pharmacist’s initial QRE documentation remains subject to the 24-hour discovery-or-notification clock.
The seven-business-day Board reporting period is measured from the date the prescription was originally written.
The manager of record must report the qualifying improper dispensing within seven business days of discovery of the related serious injury or death.
Completing the QRE record eliminates the separate serious-event report because both rules concern the same dispensing error.
The event can trigger both CQI documentation and the separate serious-event reporting pathway because the rules have different purposes and clocks.

A Massachusetts pharmacist administers an eligible patient-specific long-acting antipsychotic under the current MH/SUD pathway. Which workflow principles are consistent with the guidance? Select all that apply.
Send the administration record to the prescriber as soon after administration as practical, as strongly encouraged by DCP guidance
Allow a cashier to perform the injection after the pharmacist verifies the prescription
Skip privacy protections because the medication treats mental illness
Use a prescribed single dose supplied in eligible single-dose packaging
Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record
MA-CASE-0328

The pharmacy is using the non-vaccine medication-administration pathway in DCP 26-03-124. Personnel, patient, product, and prescription requirements are otherwise met. An administration-related reaction causes a persistent significant incapacity.

Which response accurately reflects the circular’s wording? Select ONE answer.
Immediately report the event to the prescriber; assess any separate Board reporting duties.
Appropriately communicate the reaction to the prescriber within 24 hours as the circular recommends.
Follow the prescriber’s appropriate reassessment interval; quarterly is an example rather than a universal fixed deadline.
Use professional judgment and contact the prescriber as encouraged to clarify the intended administration setting.
MA-CASE-0959
A pharmacy administers eligible ceftriaxone by the labeled IM route within the circular’s conditions.
A retail pharmacist recognizes that the circular does not create ordinary retail methadone administration for OUD outside an OTP.
MA-EXP-0366

Case A: After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.

Case B: A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.
The pharmacy may delay the serious-outcome notification for the full 24-hour routine interval.
Calling the prescriber completes every otherwise applicable Board reporting duty.
The ordinary 24-hour communication wording is a recommendation distinct from the immediate mandatory category.
Completing the report takes priority over necessary emergency care.
MA-EXP-0367

Case A: After an eligible medication injection, the patient requires additional treatment and monitoring in an emergency department; staff plan to wait 24 hours before notifying the prescriber.

Case B: A nonserious reaction in another patient is discussed under the circular's recommendation for communication within 24 hours.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.
A prescriber call does not replace a separately triggered Board report for an error or serious event.
The serious outcome requires immediate prescriber notification rather than waiting for the routine interval.
Emergency care must not be delayed while staff finish the report.

A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed no training programme of any kind. She proposes to dispense emergency contraception under the statewide standing order this week, and to dispense a COVID-19 drug under a standing order next week. How do the two proposals compare?
The emergency contraception dispensing may proceed; the COVID-19 drug may not.
The COVID-19 dispensing may proceed; the emergency contraception may not.
Both may proceed, because training is a professional expectation rather than a bar.
Neither may proceed, because both regimes require approved training beforehand.
Both may proceed once she notifies the Department that she intends to dispense.

A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.
Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.
MA-EXP-0382

Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case B? Select ONE answer.
The described statewide EC pathway requires the assumed additional course before any participation.
Using the EC standing order authorizes independent prescribing of unrelated products.
The actual intended user must be assessed through the allowed in-person or telephone pathway.
Voluntary participation eliminates every separate duty to provide access to valid prescriptions.
MA-EXP-0384

Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.
The described statewide EC pathway does not impose the additional mandatory training assumed in the first case.
Participation in this service is voluntary, while independently applicable dispensing-access duties remain.
MA-EXP-0381

Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.
The agent's request alone replaces assessment of the actual intended user for a standing-order prescription.
MA-EXP-0383

Case A: A pharmacist chooses the statewide emergency-contraception standing-order pathway but assumes an additional training course is a mandatory entry condition under that pathway.

Case B: An agent requests a standing-order prescription for someone who will take the medication, but the pharmacist has not contacted or assessed that person.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.
The standing order is a specific authority rather than a general independent prescribing license.
MA-CASE-0907

A patient requests a public-health pharmacy service in Massachusetts. Each option identifies the pathway being used; billing rules do not independently expand prescribing authority. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.
A pharmacist sells prescription-only ulipristal without an order, applying the OTC status of levonorgestrel emergency contraception.
A pharmacist confirms the applicable standing order before using its patient-specific dispensing pathway.
A pharmacist separates a plan’s extended contraception coverage from the pharmacist’s legally authorized prescribing modalities.
A pharmacist distinguishes permission to dispense under an EC standing order from a general license to prescribe any reproductive-health drug.
A pharmacist using the statewide emergency-contraception order assesses the person who will take the medication, in person or by telephone.
